content.title: About
content.content: Eggplant (Solanum melongena) is a vegetable from the nightshade family, widely cultivated in warm regions worldwide. When cooked with added fat (oil, butter) it becomes tender, silky and develops a rich flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Eggplant belongs to the same family as tomatoes, potatoes and peppers.
Its purple skin is due to anthocyanins, powerful antioxidants.
In Japan, eggplant is often used in "nasu-age", where slices are deep‑fried until crisp.
There are over 500 cultivars, varying in shape, size and skin color.
Eggplant was introduced to Europe from India in the 15th century.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber supports healthy digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Even with added fat, cooked eggplant remains relatively low‑calorie.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Anthocyanins and vitamin C help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Heart‑friendly fats
items.content: Monounsaturated fats from cooking oil can improve lipid profiles.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium aids blood‑pressure regulation and muscle function.

items.title: Nightshade allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to eggplant.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Eggplant contains oxalates, which can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible people.

items.title: High fat when fried
items.content: Excessive oil can make the dish calorie‑dense and less suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: As with many vegetables, eggplant may carry pesticide residues; wash thoroughly before cooking.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Eggplant can be sautéed, stewed, baked, or used in sauces. When cooking with oil, use olive or vegetable oil and add it toward the end to preserve flavor. Serve as a side dish, in ratatouille, casseroles, or as a crispy appetizer.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh eggplant in the refrigerator’s vegetable drawer, wrapped in a paper towel, for up to 5–7 days. Cooked eggplant should be kept in an airtight container in the fridge and consumed within 3 days.
